stronger_arguments.description: For EXP-617 (already routed, reinforced by this run): the locked formula RMSE annotation is the strongest single attack surface. A derivation does not carry a goodness-of-fit statistic against the values it allegedly derives. RMSE = 0.0071 across all 9 stations (live page line 93, fetched this run) is an open admission the three constants (0.19550, 0.1640, 32.974) were FIT to the nine published FSF values - which Section 4.2.4 already shows are themselves a globe tangent ratio. The locked formula is a 3-knob curve-fit to globe trigonometry, labelled independently derived.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome author did the verifiable parts competently here: the E001-E009 predictions were registered before the test window (predictions page: Registered 2026-03-12 | Git + OpenTimestamps anchored, raw-text/03-predictions.txt:19), the published per-station values reproduce to ~3% under V51 parameters (wins.json:WIN-044.detail_evidence), and the monitor.py Domain 10 entry honestly marks the eclipse observation PENDING with pass = None rather than faking a confirmation (monitor.py:515-519, fetched this run). Publishing a locked closed-form formula with its own RMSE (live page line 93) is also more transparency than most dome WINs offer.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Prospective registration tests the prediction in August 2026; it cannot confirm anything today, and WIN-044 counts the formula as a WIN now (wins.json:WIN-044.detail_evidence, eclipse paragraph). The reproduction succeeds only under V51 radii where FSF collapses to tan(lat)/tan(lat_BOU), a globe identity in which every dome parameter cancels (sections.json:Section-4.2.4) - and fails at 28% under the author's own V50.6 parameters (wins.json:WIN-044.finding). Transparency about the fit statistic actually undermines the derivation claim: derivations do not need RMSE values (live page line 93).
